correctness.rationale: Matrix multiplication gives [ (a,b,c),(u,v,w) ] central coordinate av-ub; using valuations x=pi^v u and y=pi^w z, zero determinant is automatic if v+w>=m, otherwise equivalently equality of reduced projective directions in P1(R/(pi^(m-v-w))). Every level-1 P1 has q+1 roots and each higher point exactly q lifts, giving a uniform projective-direction tree with same unit scalar label counts. Matching tree, unit labels and central coordinates yields a single adjacency-preserving graph bijection. The determinant map on R² has kernel size q^(m+v), giving full graph degrees q^(2m+v)-1 with multiplicities (q²-1)q^(3m-2v-2); their distinct nonuniversal degree strata recover m and universal vertices q^m recover q. The derived subgroup additive exponents p^m vs p obstruct isoclinism. Independent zero-determinant graph isomorphism for Z4 and F2[t]/t² and full degree histogram {15:48,31:12,63:4} corroborate, but infinite/general residue field proof rests on projective-reduction tree.

value.rationale: The full adjacency graph is a natural invariant of class-two Heisenberg groups; classifying exactly what it recovers and fails to recover across all finite chain rings is a substantive structural theorem, stronger than the existence of isolated nonisoclinic collisions or equality of clique-count sequences.

final_claim: For commutative finite chain rings R,S, the full element commuting graphs of UT3(R) and UT3(S) are isomorphic iff they have equal residue-field order q and nilpotency length m. The graph degree spectrum determines (q,m) and ring characteristics are not determined. For each p,m>=2 the rings Z/p^m and F_p[t]/t^m give graph-isomorphic nonisoclinic class-two groups.
